title: Constituent-Matched Composition Residual in Embodied LLM Execution

origin.rule: Outcome-derived observations may generate a new hypothesis but cannot validate it or repair the parent F0.

broad_object.question: Can task topology predict whether composing two embodied-agent tasks makes execution harder or easier?
broad_object.reason: Positive/negative subgoal interaction and goal ordering are mature planning objects; resource-bounded planning already models horizon/resource pressure; recent agent work predicts task difficulty before rollouts and uses graph/dependency structure to characterize long-horizon difficulty.
not_a_new_primitive: shared exploration as generic planning reuse
time/horizon pressure as generic resource-bounded planning

closest_work.boundary: Already predicts ex-ante task difficulty from task descriptions and structural features across agentic benchmarks; therefore absolute pre-rollout difficulty prediction is not novel.
Already models task-level agent success/difficulty using task and environment features; therefore generic success prediction is not novel.

closest_work.work: Toward Scalable Terminal Task Synthesis via Skill Graphs (SkillSynth)
closest_work.boundary: Shows graph-guided skill composition and sequential dependencies change task difficulty relative to random multi-skill composition.

closest_work.work: Graph-Structured Skill Compositions for LLM Agents (GraSP)
closest_work.boundary: Uses typed precondition/effect/data/order DAGs for long-horizon skill composition; graph structure and dependency length are already established mechanisms.
Classical planning already formalizes positive/negative subgoal interaction and serializability as determinants of combined-goal planning difficulty.
Combined conjunctive goals, positive/negative interactions, ordering and mergeability already have mature symbolic reductions.
Time, execution horizon and shared resource constraints are mature explanations for bounded-agent performance and cannot be claimed as a new composition mechanism.

narrow_residual_screen.question: After a strongest same-information model is given constituent task difficulty, proposition-weighted constituent reference, symbolic goal interaction/ordering features, graph dependency structure, and resource/horizon descriptors available before execution, is there a reproducible LLM-executor-specific residual in realized composition performance?
narrow_residual_screen.current_problem: A targeted novelty search did not identify a specific executor-side pre-outcome observable that remains distinct from ordinary bounded rationality, context/horizon pressure, task-state management, grounding/ambiguity, evaluation-budget effects, execution error, model misspecification or another task-difficulty feature.
narrow_residual_screen.strongest_same_information_reducer: A frozen model combining constituent difficulty, proposition counts, symbolic positive/negative goal interaction, room/receptacle/object overlap, dependency depth, estimated resource/horizon pressure and generic ex-ante task-difficulty features.
narrow_residual_screen.null_prediction: Once these mature reducers receive the same pre-outcome information, any apparent topology-conditioned composition sign is fully explained; adding an unnamed executor-specific residual has no held-out value.

executor_observable_search.candidate: context or prompt-state growth under composition
executor_observable_search.reduction: long-horizon context bottlenecks and context-management/folding mechanisms are already explicit research objects
refs: ICML 2026: Scaling Long-Horizon Agent via Context Folding
ICML 2026: On Training Large Language Models for Long-Horizon Tasks

executor_observable_search.candidate: task-state drift or error propagation across composed subtasks
executor_observable_search.reduction: explicit task-state management and audit loops already target propagation of incorrect state across long-horizon execution

executor_observable_search.candidate: referent/object ambiguity and fine-grained grounding burden
executor_observable_search.reduction: embodied instruction ambiguity and perception-grounding failures are already established difficulty mechanisms
refs: Seeing the details to plan ahead, 2026

executor_observable_search.candidate: shared fixed decision-call or evaluation budget under a composed task
executor_observable_search.reduction: resource-bounded planning and budget-sensitive agent benchmark decisions are mature evaluation/planning objects
refs: arXiv:2607.12338 How Many Tasks Are Enough for Agent Benchmark Decisions?

narrow_residual_screen.required_to_reopen: A future discovery must bring a materially new executor-side observable or intervention not expressible by the registered mature reducers. It must be defined before any fresh outcomes are inspected; merely renaming context length, grounding ambiguity, task-state drift, goal interaction, horizon/resource pressure or evaluation budget does not reopen this realization.
forbidden_reopen_evidence: training a predictor on outcome-derived subgroup labels and evaluating it on the same units
changing the parent MEMENTO F0 estimator or threshold
using a different model merely to obtain a favorable sign
claiming novelty from graph complexity, goal interaction, horizon pressure, or task difficulty alone
